strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: KV cache overhead in long-CoT LLMs is a significant practical bottleneck, and the paper clearly motivates the two key issues (cumulative error and RoPE distribution mismatch)

Strong empirical results: Consistent 6-8% improvements over SOTA across multiple models (7B-70B), with particularly impressive performance on aggressive 2-bit quantization where baselines fail completely

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Tests on 7 models, multiple benchmarks (AIME, CMIMC, LiveCodeBench), proper ablations, different batch sizes reflecting real memory constraints, and comparisons with three SOTA methods

Technically sound approach: The Equivalent Right Shift strategy is well-motivated with clear empirical justification (Figure 2, Table 3); integer programming formulation for block allocation is appropriate; positional interpolation application is creative
Clear presentation: Figure 1 effectively communicates the three components; method pipeline is well-structured and easy to follow
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Each component combines existing techniques—progressive bit-width reduction is straightforward, block-wise allocation via sensitivity analysis is standard practice, and positional interpolation is directly from Chen et al. (2023). The main contribution is combining known techniques for this specific application

Fake quantization only (critical limitation): All experiments use simulated quantization, not actual low-precision kernels. Real quantized inference may have different numerical properties; progressive shrinking at runtime may not be efficient with optimized kernels; no latency/throughput measurements despite practical deployment claims; severely limits assessment of real-world applicability
Incomplete scope: Explicitly excludes Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) used in DeepSeek-V2 and modern models; only tests GQA/MQA; limits generalizability across contemporary architectures

Weak positional interpolation contribution: Table 4 shows only 1.66% improvement with s=4; performance degradation at s=16 is unexplained; ablation limited to single model; unclear if improvements are significant given sampling variance with only 30-problem benchmarks

Experimental design choices lack justification: Different batch sizes for different methods (PM-KVQ BS=32 vs KIVI BS=32,40) complicates direct comparison; calibration dataset (512 samples from RedPajama) has no ablation on sensitivity to data selection; integer programming overhead claimed 'negligible' without timing data

Architectural generalization concerns: Figures 3-4 reveal Qwen models have high first-block sensitivity while LLaMA doesn't, but this difference is unexplained; raises questions about whether method generalizes across model families

Positional Interpolation evaluation incomplete: Results show modest gains; no principled method for selecting scaling factor s; unexplained performance degradation at higher s values limits confidence in this component

Reproducibility issues: Code URL missing from abstract ('available at .'); missing timing measurements for integer programming solver; insufficient documentation of hyperparameter selection (α grid search details)

Statistical rigor: Large standard deviations in some results; no significance testing; some improvements may be within noise margins; voting accuracy averages multiple samples, which doesn't reflect single-sample deployment scenarios

Limited analysis of failure modes: MiKV/RotateKV failing completely on 2-bit quantization is mentioned but not investigated; would benefit from understanding why methods fail and whether improvements are possible

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the practical KV cache bottleneck in long-CoT reasoning LLMs
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model scales (7B-70B) with multiple reasoning benchmarks and ablation studies
Significant practical improvements showing up to 8% accuracy gains at extreme compression ratios (2-bit/4-bit)
Clear problem articulation with good intuition about RoPE's frequency-dependent channel behavior and cumulative quantization error
Pragmatic engineering solutions including positional interpolation to avoid O(N²) calibration costs
weaknesses: Limited novelty: progressive quantization, block-wise allocation, and positional interpolation largely combine or directly adapt existing techniques without fundamental new insights

Critical evaluation limitation: all experiments use 'fake quantization' rather than actual int4/int2 implementations, undermining claims about memory savings, inference speedup, and practical deployment
Missing essential metrics: no actual memory consumption, inference latency, or throughput measurements reported, only accuracy metrics
Questionable experimental design: different batch sizes used for different components (BS=32 vs BS=40) making fair comparison difficult and appearing designed to demonstrate the method works

Narrow evaluation scope: limited to mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks; restricted to GQA-based models; excludes MLA architecture used in DeepSeek-V2; not evaluated on general long-context tasks

Methodological concerns: rough first-order Taylor approximation for sensitivity without validation that metric correlates with performance; Table 4 shows positional interpolation can hurt (s=16 degrades performance) with no adequate explanation

Technical justification gaps: 'Equivalent Right Shift' formula (Eq. 3) presented without derivation; block-wise allocation uses standard resource allocation; design choices (why B={4,8} vs B={2,4}, why store first+128 tokens in INT16) lack clear justification

Missing critical analyses: why baselines completely fail (0% accuracy) on 2-bit Qwen-7B while PM-KVQ succeeds unexplained; no investigation of which components matter most; calibration cost vs. inference savings trade-off not quantified
Incomplete reproducibility: code URL missing; hyperparameter choices (s=4, α grid search, group size 128) lack justification; computational cost of integer programming solver not discussed
Statistical rigor issues: no significance testing despite reporting ± std dev; some improvements (0.84%, 1.66%) potentially within noise margins; multiple comparisons without correction

strengths: Addresses a practically important and timely problem: KV cache memory overhead in long-CoT LLMs, which is increasingly critical for emerging models like DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI-o1
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model sizes (7B-70B) with strong and consistent improvements (up to 8%) over SOTA baselines (KIVI, RotateKV, MiKV)

Well-designed technical components: progressive quantization is intuitive and practical; block-wise allocation via integer programming is principled; positional interpolation cleverly avoids additional overhead
Excellent empirical validation including detailed ablation studies (bit-width shrinking strategies, positional interpolation effects) and sensitivity analysis across transformer blocks
Strong robustness demonstrated through voting accuracy improvements and stability across diverse batch sizes and memory configurations
Clear presentation with well-motivated introduction and informative figures, particularly Figure 1 illustrating the three proposed techniques
Practical implementation details well-thought-out, particularly the 'Equivalent Right Shift' strategy for bit-width shrinking
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: individual components (progressive quantization, sensitivity-based mixed-precision allocation, positional interpolation) are not novel; main contribution is combining existing techniques for long-CoT domain, which feels incremental for a top-tier venue

Calibration dataset concerns: only 512 samples from arXiv (academic papers); no sensitivity analysis on how calibration data choice affects results; unclear generalization to other domains beyond math/code reasoning
Incomplete baseline comparisons: SKVQ [6] (sliding window KV quantization) not compared despite relevance; missing comparisons with recent efficient inference methods

Weak justification for positional interpolation: modest improvement (1.66% in Table 4); unclear why s=4 (8K effective length) adequately approximates 32K distribution; s=16 degrades performance with limited explanation; lacks theoretical analysis

Evaluation methodology concerns: uses fake quantization rather than actual low-bit operations; modest sample sizes (16 for math, 4 for code); large error bars with no statistical significance testing; multiple comparisons without correction

Limited scope and generalization: experiments nearly exclusively on DeepSeek models (except one QwQ-32B); only reasoning/math/code tasks; method doesn't support MLA (multi-head latent attention used in DeepSeek-V2), limiting applicability to newer models

Block-wise allocation analysis incomplete: standard integer programming formulation with limited novelty; no computational cost analysis; insufficient ablation comparing block-wise vs. uniform allocation; sensitivity measurements use first-order Taylor approximation ignoring interaction effects

Reproducibility issues: code link is blank; calibration data selection underspecified; missing inference latency measurements; bit-width shrinking trigger mechanism (deterministic vs. adaptive) unclear

Missing important experimental comparisons: no evaluation on other long-CoT models beyond DeepSeek/QwQ; no comparison with SKVQ; no evaluation on non-reasoning long-context tasks (retrieval, summarization); limited calibration robustness analysis

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear identification of why existing methods fail on long-CoT LLMs (cumulative error and RoPE distribution mismatch)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model sizes (7B-70B), architectures, and benchmarks with consistent improvements (up to 8% accuracy over SOTA)
Thorough ablation studies validating each component (bit-width shrinking strategies, block sensitivity, positional interpolation effectiveness)
Technically sound approach with formal Integer Programming formulation for block-wise allocation and mathematical proof of Equivalent Right Shift strategy
Practical contribution addressing real bottleneck in long-context LLM deployment with promised code release
Strong empirical results demonstrating 2.73-5.18× throughput improvement over 16-bit models and generalization to short-context tasks
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: each component (mixed-precision allocation, progressive quantization, positional interpolation) builds on existing techniques; primary contribution is combining them

Experimental methodology concerns: (1) uses fake quantization (float32 simulation) instead of actual int2/int4 implementations, missing practical performance characteristics; (2) unequal batch sizes across methods complicate direct comparison; (3) unfair baseline comparisons where MiKV/RotateKV completely fail at 2-bit

Insufficient mechanistic analysis: lacks quantitative characterization of cumulative error contribution, explanation for why deeper blocks are more sensitive, and detailed sensitivity computation methodology
Significant calibration overhead not fully addressed: pre-inference procedures require 17-120 minutes; grid search for α adds 52-408 minutes; total cost comparison with baselines missing
Positional interpolation design choices inadequately justified: fixed s=4 choice lacks rationale; Table 5 shows method is sensitive to s (s=16 hurts performance); unclear how to select s in practice

Limited scope and reproducibility concerns: only two model families tested; MLA attention and sparse attention not properly evaluated; gradient-based sensitivity computation details missing; some hyperparameters appear ad-hoc

Statistical significance issues: overlapping error bars in many results; some improvements marginal relative to error margins; unclear if differences are statistically significant across multiple runs

Incomplete technical exposition: Integer Programming formulation lacks clarity on Mem(·) computation; choice of L1 norm for sensitivity not justified; missing analysis of layer normalization effects on gradients

strengths: Addresses important and practical problem: KV cache overhead in long-CoT LLMs is a genuine bottleneck with 10-100GB memory requirements
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple model sizes (7B-70B), diverse benchmarks (AIME, CMIMC, LiveCode, IFEval), and detailed ablation studies
Achieves strong empirical results on reasoning benchmarks: up to 8% accuracy improvement over SOTA on mathematical reasoning under aggressive quantization
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-structured methodology; detailed experimental setup enhances reproducibility
Proposes practical solutions combining progressive quantization, sensitivity-based allocation, and positional interpolation that work well in combination
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Progressive quantization is straightforward engineering, block-wise allocation directly applies existing techniques (Li et al. 2023), and positional interpolation is borrowed from Chen et al. 2023 without significant adaptation
Unfair baseline comparisons: RotateKV and MiKV achieve 0% on 2-bit Qwen-7B, raising questions about whether these methods are designed for such extreme quantization or if implementations are correct
Negative practical speedup: Table 3 shows PM-KVQ is 2.45-16.18% slower than KIVI baseline, significantly undermining practical applicability despite efficiency claims

Incomplete analysis of core claims: (1) 'Large cumulative error' lacks empirical evidence (no error curves); (2) Positional interpolation shows only 1.66% improvement and performance drops at s=16; (3) Contribution from INT16 first/recent tokens (common across methods) not isolated
Narrow scope and limited generalizability: Only DeepSeek and QwQ tested; doesn't handle MLA; heavy focus on mathematical reasoning tasks; missing comparisons with other long-context approaches
Fake quantization only: All experiments use fake quantization without actual low-bit CUDA kernel implementation, limiting validation of efficiency claims
Limited block-wise allocation gains: Improvements often small; for Qwen-7B BS32→40 change (disabling allocation) causes minimal degradation, questioning practical value of this component

Missing technical depth: Equivalent Right Shift strategy requires complex proof but ablation tested on only one model; RoPE distribution mismatch claim lacks empirical evidence with data distribution plots
Hyperparameter sensitivity: Positional interpolation factor s is critical but sparsely evaluated; pre-inference overhead of 13-120 minutes substantial but minimally discussed

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly articulates why existing KV cache quantization methods fail for long-CoT LLMs due to cumulative error and short-context calibration limitations
Strong and comprehensive experiments: Evaluates 7B-70B models on multiple benchmarks (AIME, CMIMC, LiveCode, IFEval) with consistent 8% improvements and 2.73-5.18× throughput gains

Novel technical combination: While individual components exist, the integration of progressive quantization, block-wise allocation, and positional interpolation is well-motivated for long-CoT scenarios
Elegant mathematical contributions: Equivalent Right Shift strategy (Eq. 3) is clever with formal proof; Integer Programming formulation for block allocation is principled
Thorough ablation studies: Tables 4-5 and Figures 3-4 validate each component; particularly convincing on bit-width shrinking strategies comparison
Impressive performance at extreme quantization: Achieves 64.79% vs 51.88% (KIVI) on 70B model at 2-bit, where baselines fail completely
Reproducibility: Public datasets, code promised, detailed experimental setup, extensive appendices with implementation details
weaknesses: Limited individual technical novelty: Progressive quantization is intuitive but straightforward; block-wise allocation and positional interpolation adapt existing techniques; main contribution is their combination

Throughput overhead underexplored: Table 3 shows 16% slowdown vs KIVI (424.72 vs 506.72 tokens/s) but paper claims overhead is negligible without detailed analysis of causes or potential optimizations

Positional interpolation lacks rigor: Scaling factor s fixed at 4 with limited exploration (Table 5); no principled guidance for choosing s; connection between s=4 (8K length) and actual 54K-token channel period undefined

Progressive quantization benefits not quantified: Missing empirical analysis of cumulative error reduction; Table 12 shows variable response lengths but lacks breakdown of when progressive quantization helps vs uniform Fbit

Evaluation scope limitations: Only DeepSeek-R1-Distill and QwQ tested; MLA attention mechanism explicitly excluded but increasingly important; KVTuner comparison limited to one model; fake quantization vs real INT kernels
Integer Programming overhead: Pre-inference costs 22.5-23.5% (Table 11); bit-width set B restricted to {2,4} or {4,8}; no guidance for choosing B for new models
Block sensitivity analysis incomplete: Figures 3-4 show variation across models (Qwen vs LLaMA) but no explanation of causes or prediction for new models
Comparison fairness: Different batch sizes for different methods and different GPUs make throughput comparisons less direct; baselines completely fail at 2-bit limiting informativeness
